intro.title: Build a debounced search input
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a search input field that delays sending requests until the user stops typing, preventing excessive API calls. You'll learn about the core programming concept of debouncing, which helps optimize performance by grouping rapid events into a single action. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, event listeners, and the setTimeout and clearTimeout methods. By the end, you'll have a functional, efficient search component that improves user experience in real-time applications.
intro.usecase: Debounced search inputs are essential in modern web applications where real-time filtering is required without overwhelming servers or degrading user experience. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce sites like Amazon or eBay, where search suggestions appear as you type without sending excessive API requests. Dashboard interfaces with live data filtering, such as analytics tools or admin panels, use debouncing to smoothly update charts and tables. Even social media platforms implement debounced search when filtering friends lists or searching through posts, ensuring responsive UI while managing network efficiency.
